transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-29
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Ravi Suresh (Redwood DevAdv); Liam O'Connor, Priya Sharma, Derek Ng, Ana Ruiz (Riverbend)

Summary:
Quickstart walkthrough for Redwood SDKs (Python + TypeScript), focusing on auth patterns for a regulated finance customer, environment setup (VPC/staging), Console usage for routing and Optimize hints, and next steps to run a short benchmark on staging. Security questions around KMS and SSO were raised.

Topics covered:
- SDK install (pip/npm) and auth methods (API key, SSO/SAML, token rotation)
- Env variables, CI secrets, sample pipeline for deploying a small endpoint
- Console: routes, keys, per-route cost view, and setting up Optimize recommendations
- Private/Dedicated considerations: VPC peering, data residency, SOC2 audit artifacts

Action items (as discussed):
- See action_items in metadata

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is Jordan from Redwood, i'm gonna hand off to Maya who will run through the quickstart and then we'll circle back for questions.
[00:23] Maya Chen: yeah hi hi, thanks liam and team. i'll start with the Python quickstart; for Riverbend we prepped a tiny example that uses prefix caching and shows a basic generation call. first step pip install redwood-client, or for TS npm i @redwood/inference — the packages are deliberately small.
[00:46] Priya Sharma: sorry, just to interrupt, is the package name exactly @redwood/inference? our internal naming conventions...
[00:51] Maya Chen: yeah correct — sorry it's a placeholder in the repo, the real npm name we shared in the invite doc, link is in the slack thread. (laughter)
[01:05] Maya Chen: for auth, we show two patterns: short-lived SSO-issued tokens (via OIDC/SAML) and API key fallback for non-interactive services. the recommended pattern for Riverbend (given you have an internal SSO) is to mint short-lived tokens with your identity provider and exchange for Redwood session tokens with our auth endpoint — helps with rotation and audit logs.
[01:35] Derek Ng: can you say more about the KMS piece? we need to keep model inputs encrypted at rest.
[01:40] Maya Chen: absolutely. on Private/Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS/HSM — we support AWS KMS + external HSM via PKCS#11. if you're on Hosted API we do server-side encryption and can bring-your-own-key for encryption at rest; all calls are logged in audit trails visible in Console. we have SOC2 artifacts and an encryption whitepaper i'll share.
[02:06] Liam O'Connor: ok good, we will need that whitepaper. next, the code.
[02:12] Maya Chen: quick snippet — Python: from redwood import RedwoodClient ; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) ; resp = client.generate("Summarize quarterly backup logs") ; print(resp.text). for TS: import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference' ; const c = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }) ; await c.generate({ prompt: '...'}). we also include typed defs for response shapes.
[02:50] Priya Sharma: how do we pass per-request routing? we want some requests on Dedicated and others on Hosted for cost reasons.
[02:56] Maya Chen: great question — the SDK supports an optional route param (route: 'dedicated:rb-finance-v1' or 'hosted:default'), you can also set per-service config via env vars. Console exposes per-route dashboards so you can trace tokens and latency.
[03:20] Ravi Suresh: small caveat — the route names in the example are symbolic; real route IDs come from the Console once an admin creates them.
[03:28] Ana Ruiz: what's the expected latency for the small models? we need sub-200ms p50 for certain workflows.
[03:35] Maya Chen: for small generation models we routinely hit 80–150ms p50 on Dedicated; Hosted varies by region. we'll run a bench on your staging env to confirm. for strict SLOs we recommend Dedicated with a reserved pool.
[03:52] Liam O'Connor: about CI/CD — we want to rotate keys without downtime. any recommended pipeline?
[03:58] Maya Chen: yes, typical pattern: store REDWOOD_API_KEY in your CI secrets manager with a short TTL, use a sidecar to fetch rotated tokens, or you can do an OIDC dance in your CI to mint tokens and swap. our examples include a GitHub Actions job that rotates keys and updates env secrets.
[04:21] Priya Sharma: can we do local dev without hitting production tokens?
[04:25] Jordan Patel: yes we provide a lite dev key with rate limits plus a local mocking helper in the repo so you can run without hitting costs.
[04:33] Maya Chen: switching to Console demo — showing the project, routes, and the Optimize tab. Optimize will surface quantization and batching suggestions based on observed token distribution; it recommends a quantization profile and batching size for lower latency and cost.
[04:55] Priya Sharma: is Optimize agent-driven or manual?
[04:58] Maya Chen: it's suggestions-first; you can run a recommended change in a canary route. it will also show expected cost delta.
[05:10] Derek Ng: any compliance flags from Optimize? like does it show data retention impacts?
[05:14] Maya Chen: yep it flags retention windows; and you can set retention per-route in Console to control ephemeral KV cache TTLs for privacy.
[05:27] Liam O'Connor: on Private, we need VPC peering and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. how's the network setup?
[05:33] Jordan Patel: for Private we do a control-plane handshake over a management VPC, then data plane either tunnels via peering or sits on-prem. we support VPC peering and private link. audit logs can be shipped via syslog or S3 with object-level encryption.
[05:50] Priya Sharma: does Redwood store any PII by default?
[05:53] Maya Chen: default is ephemeral cache; we do not persist customer prompt data beyond configured retention unless you opt into longer storage for evals. you can also disable KV caching.
[06:06] Ana Ruiz: quick question on billing and per-route bucketing — can we label routes by business unit?
[06:11] Jordan Patel: yes tags + per-route billing is supported; Console shows token-level cost breakdown by tag.
[06:18] Liam O'Connor: let's walk through the quickstart in the repo — maybe share screen?
[06:22] Maya Chen: sure i'll share. (screen share noise)
[06:35] Maya Chen: repo layout: quickstart/python/README.md, quickstart/typescript/README.md, examples/ci, examples/console-setup, docs/auth.md. the README has step-by-step env var examples: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_ROUTE, REDWOOD_REGION.
[06:55] Priya Sharma: for TS types — are they strongly typed for response shapes? we need deterministic parsing in our pipeline.
[07:02] Maya Chen: yes response types include tokens, choices, and a structured output helper. there's an open schema for structured outputs — we include zod schemas in the TS package.
[07:14] Ravi Suresh: mention about the KV cache: when you enable prefix caching for a chat history it keeps KV entries for X minutes; you can change TTL per-route. no persistent PII unless you set persistence.
[07:28] Derek Ng: ok. security folks want to see SAML metadata and SCIM provisioning — can you send the SAML metadata?
[07:33] Jordan Patel: yes we'll attach SAML metadata and a SCIM guide.
[07:37] Maya Chen: the SAML flow we show: user authenticates via Okta -> Okta issues assertion -> our auth endpoint exchanges assertion for session token -> SDK gets ephemeral token. we recommend enforced MFA on identity provider side.
[07:55] Priya Sharma: any rate limiting patterns? we have bursts at month-end.
[07:58] Maya Chen: burst capacity is supported on Dedicated; Hosted has soft quotas. you can set autoscaling policies and a burst window for Reserved pools.
[08:13] Liam O'Connor: about the bench test — how should we instrument traces?
[08:17] Maya Chen: include the X-Request-Id header; Console will surface traces and token/latency breakdowns per request. we also have a small tracing lib you can drop into your app to correlate logs with request ids.
[08:31] Priya Sharma: you'll share a sample policy for canarying changes?
[08:34] Maya Chen: yes, a snippet: create new route canary:v2, set 10% traffic weight for canary in Console, run traffic for 24–72 hours, check cost/quality metrics, then promote.
[08:50] Ana Ruiz: what's the expected timeline to go from pilot to Dedicated?
[08:54] Jordan Patel: typically 4–8 weeks: initial pilot + benching (1–2 weeks), security review and SSO (1–2 weeks), provisioning Dedicated pool (1–2 weeks). depends on procurement.
[09:08] Liam O'Connor: procurement will need a contract addendum for data residency.
[09:12] Jordan Patel: noted, i'll pass to legal and include the residency clause.
[09:17] Priya Sharma: can you show the env var example for the GH Actions job?
[09:20] Maya Chen: sure, here's a snippet we put in examples/ci:
  - name: Set REDWOOD token
    uses: aws-actions/aws-secretsmanager-get@v1
    with: secret: redwood/dev/api-key
  - name: Run tests
    run: REDWOOD_API_KEY=${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY }} python -m pytest
(voice overlap)
[09:45] Derek Ng: about audit logs format — do you have a sample? we prefer JSONL.
[09:50] Maya Chen: yep JSONL and we can forward to your S3 in compressed chunks.
[09:55] Ravi Suresh: small note — some customers refer to our product as Redwood Inference API, some as Redwood Platform; in the docs you'll see both — it's the same product.
[10:06] Ana Ruiz: any gotchas for local dev on windows?
[10:09] Maya Chen: the local mock uses POSIX paths in examples; if you're on Windows switch to WSL or adjust path separators. we flagged that in README.
[10:18] Liam O'Connor: ok let's surface the actual quickstart link and the staging access.
[10:22] Jordan Patel: link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstart-py-ts (private repo). staging access we need Liam to share a Bastion host IP and an IAM role.
[10:35] Priya Sharma: regarding testing — for regression checks we want deterministic outputs for small prompts; does Redwood offer a deterministic mode?
[10:40] Maya Chen: we have a low-temperature plus deterministic sampling option for certain model builds; it's model-dependent but we can pin a model version and seed.
[10:48] Liam O'Connor: perfect. final questions from procurement?
[10:52] Ana Ruiz: procurement asked about SLAs for Dedicated — what do we offer?
[10:55] Jordan Patel: Dedicated has a 99.9% uptime SLA for the data plane and a latency SLO we can attach per contract. I'll include the SLA doc.
[11:05] Priya Sharma: great — time for next steps?
[11:08] Jordan Patel: recap: we'll share quickstart repo, SAML + SCIM docs, SOC2 + encryption whitepaper, Dedicated pricing. Maya will provide the auth-runbook and canary snippet. Liam will create staging VPC and share access. we'll aim for the bench test next Tuesday.
[11:26] Ana Ruiz: thanks all. good meeting.

(End of recording)
